subject: Tailwind SLA characterization — test matrix and methodology
messages:
From: Sara Kline <sara.k@tailwind.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez
Cc: Tailwind Procurement <procurement@tailwind.ai>, Ben Chu <bchu@tailwind.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Section 6 (performance characterization)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the quick RFP turnaround. Our engineering team dug into Section 6 (performance characterization) and asked for more precise definitions so we can validate SLAs during our bakeoff. Can you confirm the following items so we can finalize the test plan on our side?

1) Exact model binary / flavor you expect us to benchmark against (model name + quantization if any).
2) The recommended request mix (prompt length distribution: short/medium/long) and percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls.
3) Guidance on warmup policy for cold-start measurements (how long to run warmup and whether to keep KV-cache warm between runs).
4) Preferred GPU/hardware baseline for comparisons (family + vRAM) and what fallbacks are allowed for Dedicated runs.
5) The telemetry artifacts you need from us to consider the run "valid" (logs, token-level timings, kernel traces, sample requests).

We want the acceptance criteria to be unambiguous: specific QPS targets, p50/p95/p99 latencies for both interactive (single-request) and batch-mode workloads, and clear instructions for how to handle transient spikes.

Can you reply with a short test matrix and the artifact list? If possible, a single-sheet spreadsheet would be easiest.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kline
Head of Infrastructure, Tailwind.ai

[attachment: tailwind_rfp_questions.pdf (pdf)]
From: mateo_alvarez
To: Sara Kline <sara.k@tailwind.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park, vivek_kulkarni
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on Section 6 (performance characterization)

Sara —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise test matrix and the artifacts we require to consider a run valid. I've looped in Kim (performance lead) and Vivek (runtime/product) to attach the spreadsheet and sample logs.

Quick summary (high level):
- Model: redwood/gptx-7b (fp16) and redwood/gptx-7b-q4_0 (INT4 quantized) — we ask you to run both if you plan to evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Hardware baseline: NVIDIA A10G (48GB) for single-GPU baseline; A100-40GB as optional upper-bound. Report which GPU was used for each run.
- Request mix (short/med/long): 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-512 tokens), 10% long (513-2048 tokens). Streaming calls: 25% of requests in the interactive mix.
- Warmup: 10 minutes sustained at 50% of target QPS, then ramp to target for 5 minutes before measurement window. KV-cache: keep warm between runs for steady-state; cold-start runs should be performed separately and labeled.
- Measurement windows: 30 minutes steady-state window per QPS point, with at least three repeats.

Acceptance criteria (examples you can use to grade pass/fail):
- Interactive single-request (no batching): target qps points: 10, 50, 200. Report p50/p95/p99 latencies for request end-to-end (client-observed) and token-level generation time. Pass if p95 <= 200ms at qps=50 on A10G for fp16.
- Batch generation (batch-size 8, server-side batching): points: 100, 500, 2000 concurrent inflight. Report throughput (tokens/s), GPU util, and token-level latency distribution.
- Tail behavior: provide p99.9 and 99.99 if possible; if not, include empirical max over the steady window.

Required artifacts:
- request-logs-sample.jsonl (token timestamps, request id, model flavor, GPU id)
- prom-metrics-export.txt (preferably Prometheus scrape for the run window)
- kernel-trace-summary.txt (optional but useful)
- tailwind_rfp_section6_test_matrix.xlsx (single-sheet matrix with QPS points, payload distribution, hardware, model)

I'll let Kim attach the spreadsheet and recommend instrumentation tweaks. Vivek, please add any runtime caveats or fallback notes.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park
To: mateo_alvarez, Sara Kline <sara.k@tailwind.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni
Date: 2026-10-29T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on Section 6 (performance characterization)

Mateo / Sara —

Attached is the test matrix spreadsheet (single sheet) and a small sample of request logs we usually ask customers to provide. Notes below correspond to rows in the matrix.

[attachment: tailwind_rfp_section6_test_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
[attachment: request-logs-sample.jsonl (jsonl)]

Key notes / clarifications:
- Model mapping: we used the internal alias redwood/gptx-7b-fp16 and redwood/gptx-7b-q4_0 for the spreadsheet. If you are referencing an externally hosted model name, map it to one of those flavors before running.
- Client-observed latency: measure from first client byte sent to final newline (or EOS) received.
- Streaming: for streaming measurement, report average per-token send interval and end-to-end time separately.
- Batching policy: server-side batching should be disabled for "interactive single-request" rows and enabled for "batch" rows. Indicate whether a run used continuous batching (dynamic) or micro-batching with fixed-size windows.
- Cold-start protocol: reboot the worker pool between cold-start runs and record system boot timestamps. Cold starts should be labeled explicitly and excluded from steady-state aggregates.
- Noise filtering: exclude maintenance windows and known noisy host IDs. Provide prom label host_id and a small exclude list if present.

Metrics/columns we expect in the spreadsheet (already included):
- run_id, model_flavor, gpu_family, qps_target, payload_distribution, streaming_pct, batch_mode, batch_size, warmup_duration_s, measurement_duration_s, repeat_index, notes

Deliverables checklist for an accepted run:
- Spreadsheet populated and signed off by Tailwind engineer (Google Drive link).
- request-logs-sample.jsonl for each measurement window.
- Prometheus scrape (.txt) covering warmup + measurement windows.
- A brief results summary (1 page) noting pass/fail vs acceptance criteria and any anomalies.

If this looks good I propose we schedule a one-hour joint run on Nov 4 to execute a single QPS sweep and compare results live. Sara — does 11/4 10:00 PT work for you?

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni
To: Sara Kline <sara.k@tailwind.ai>, mateo_alvarez
Cc: kimberly_park
Date: 2026-10-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on Section 6 (performance characterization)

Sara — quick runtime notes and a couple of caveats before the joint run:

1) Quantization caveat: INT4 (q4_0) gives cost savings but can increase generation variance. When you run q4_0, please include per-request loss/quality samples (5–10 prompts) so we can correlate any latency anomalies with output quality.

2) Fallbacks: if your Dedicated pool runs out of capacity mid-run, the automatic routing may failover to a smaller instance family. Please flag any such events in the spreadsheet; we will not include failover-influenced windows in steady-state aggregates.

3) Kernel-level traces: we do not require full kernel traces for initial validation — a kernel-trace-summary.txt with timestamps and high-level events is sufficient. If you see unexpected p99 spikes, we will request deeper traces.

4) Scale strategy recommendation: for the scalability rows (500–2000 concurrent), prefer horizontal sharding across 2–4 replicas rather than single-GPU scale-up — this better reflects how Dedicated pools behave and produces more stable tail statistics.

Action items before the Nov 4 run:
- Tailwind: populate the spreadsheet and upload the sample logs to the Drive link Kim provided.
- Redwood (Kim + me): prepare a short run checklist and a Prometheus scrape template.
- Schedule: Mateo to confirm 11/4 10:00 PT with Sara.

Thanks — looking forward to the joint validation.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
